title: And some of the best American accents I’ve heard come out of the UK! ...
transcript: I was recently invited to the premiere of the Bonnie and Clyde Pro Shot that you can now rent. So let's talk about it. First of all, this is my first time ever seeing Bonnie and Clyde. I didn't see it when I was on Broadway. They recently had the West End production that stemmed from this concert that I also missed. So I was really excited to finally see this show in full. And this is the capture of a two day concert that they did in the UK, starring Jeremy Jordan as Clyde and Francis May, Lea McCann as Bonnie. And they together are tremendous. And I say concert very loosely because this is a fully staged concert. That's more staged than, like, any encores! Production that I've seen. There's no binders, it's fully memorized. They have costumes, there's a set, there's, like, even some choreography. Like, this feels like a full, minimalist production of Bonnie and Clyde, and this is a really good capture. There are some moments where I felt like we were getting too many edits in a song that I just wanted the camera to stay still. But there's some really fantastic angles in this. And the fact that they only shot it over the two days that they did this concert is incredible. And I'm just so happy that we have this, like, recorded so that everyone can watch it. Of course, Bonnie and Clyde isn't a perfect musical. There's definitely some things I Would have done differently, but I. It's incredibly entertaining, and I'm very glad that we have it, like, immortalized. There's definitely some subplots that I wish we dove into a little more, like, why did Blanche get roped into all of this? And then there's some subplots that I wish we dove into a little less, like the cop that's in love with Bonnie. That just made me laugh every time he opened his mouth. But then it's all paid off when you get some slam dunk moments, like, raise a little hell and dying ain't so bad. That just, uh. There they hit. And then after the premiere, they did have a talk back with Jeremy Jordan, Francis Maely McCann, and Natalie McQueen, who plays Blanche in the pro shot, as well as Frank Wildhorn, the composer, and Ivan Menshall, the book writer. And as somebody who constantly criticizes books, I am really loving getting to hear from book writers, their, like, intentions and their interpretations of the source material in, like, putting together the story that they do. Because Ivan Mitchell spoke a lot about how he wanted to focus on the. The story and the motivations for why they did the crimes as opposed to the crimes. And that's definitely differently from how I would have approached the material, but I really respect that he, like, had that vision and stuck to it, and I hope this trend continues. I hope we get to hear more from Book writers in the future on, you know, the work that they are writing and what their thought process is in writing that. Most incredible part about this talk back, though, was when they talked about the rehearsal process, because like I said, this was a two day concert only. They had five days of rehearsal and Jeremy Jordan didn't even show up until day three. So they really only had three days of rehearsal to basically stage this full show. I, I am shook. The cast was even shook that they, they did it in that amount of time. I definitely don't think that should be a trend and, you know, let actors do what they're capable of, but credit where credit is due. That is freaking incredible. Are you kidding me? Now, we have this absolutely fantastic capture of Bonnie and Clyde and I, I just wish that we would do this with more shows, put up, you know, stage concerts just so we can get a capture so people can see the full book and score of a musical with fantastic performances. I want this to be a trend and I wish that more shows were able to do this. And unfortunately, the fact of the matter is, it's just cheaper to do this in the UK. But I, I, I look at something like this absolutely stellar capture of Bonnie and Clyde and I go, why can't we film every single encores production? Why Can't we film every single Kennedy Center concert? Uh, and I just, uh. I wish that we saw more of this in the States, and I hope that we see more of this in general in the future. Because at the end of the day, it all comes down to money, and that's a whole other conversation. But I just. I love seeing stuff like this, and I hope that we see more of it. If you wanna watch the pro shot, it is available to rent at Bonnie Clyde live.com for $15 without ads or $10 with ads. Uh, but the ads are only at the beginning and the intermission of the show. So just do it with the ads, save the five bucks. Um, but it's available then for 30 days after you rent it. So, um, definitely check that out if you're interested. And I am just so happy that we have this musical captured for more people to see it. And I really hope that this trend continues.
